title: Business taxes in Mauritius
summary: The taxes a business in Mauritius meets on its profits: income tax on companies and the levies charged with it, how a sole trader and a société are taxed instead, and how and when to file and pay. Figures are those in force on 20 November 2026, after the Finance Act 2026.
audience: Owners of companies, partners and sole traders, including first-time business owners.

facts.label: Company income tax, standard rate
facts.detail: On chargeable income. Rate in force on 20 November 2026.

facts.label: Company income tax on export of goods
facts.detail: On the share of chargeable income that comes from exporting goods: export income over total gross income. In force since 1 July 2017.

facts.label: Partial exemption
facts.detail: Foreign dividends, interest earned by a company that is not a bank or other listed financial business, and others. 95% for interest earned by a collective investment scheme or closed-end fund. Substance conditions apply.

facts.label: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Fund
facts.value: 2% of the previous year's chargeable income
facts.detail: At least 75% is paid to the MRA. For a CSR Fund set up in calendar year 2026 the share is at least 50%.

facts.label: Corporate Climate Responsibility (CCR) levy
facts.value: 2% of chargeable income, where turnover is above MUR 50 million
facts.detail: Turnover is gross income from all sources, exempt income included. Applies from the year of assessment that started on 1 July 2024.

facts.label: Fair Share Contribution, companies
facts.value: 5% of chargeable income, or 2% for a company taxed at 3%, where chargeable income is above MUR 24 million
facts.detail: On the whole chargeable income of the accounting year, not only the part above the test. Income derived from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028.

facts.label: Advance Payment System (APS) threshold
facts.detail: Quarterly statements are due where last year's gross income was above MUR 10 million and the company had chargeable income.

facts.label: APS statements and payment
facts.value: Within 3 months of the end of each of the first three quarters
facts.detail: Counted from the end of the month in which the quarter ends. Tax is worked on a quarter of last year's chargeable income, or on the quarter's own figures.

facts.label: Company annual return and payment
facts.value: Within 6 months of the year end
facts.detail: Counted from the end of the month in which the accounting period ends. June and December year ends have set dates.

facts.label: Due dates at the end of June and December
facts.value: 2 days earlier, excluding Saturdays and public holidays
facts.detail: For APS quarters ending in March and September, and for the returns of companies with June and December year ends.

facts.label: Sole trader
facts.detail: On the bands for individuals, after personal deductions. The return is due by 15 October.

facts.label: Income tax bands for individuals, including sole traders
facts.detail: First MUR 500,000 at 0%, next MUR 500,000 at 10%, next MUR 11 million at 20%, remainder at 35%. Income year starting 1 July 2026. Our guide to personal income tax has the deductions.

facts.label: Resident société or partnership
facts.value: Not taxed itself: each associate pays on a share
facts.detail: The société pays CSR at 2% of the previous year's net income, and the CCR levy when its turnover passes the test. Its return is due by 30 September.

facts.label: Presumptive tax for small enterprises
facts.value: 1% of gross income, where gross income is MUR 10 million or less
facts.detail: Optional, in farming, forestry, fishing, manufacturing, retail or wholesale of goods. Income from other sources must be MUR 400,000 or less.

facts.label: Late payment of income tax
facts.detail: From 1 July 2025. The penalty is 1% for a small enterprise with turnover of MUR 10 million or less.

blocks.text: The Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) runs these taxes on a self-assessment basis. The business works out its own tax, files a return at the end of each period and pays what the return shows. The MRA can audit a return, and can act where no return is filed. A person resident in Mauritius is taxed on worldwide income. A non-resident is taxed on income from sources in Mauritius.

blocks.text: Tax rules change each year with the Budget and the Finance Act. The Finance Act 2026 was assented to on 12 August 2026. The figures in this guide are taken from the Income Tax Act and the Value Added Tax Act as consolidated by the MRA up to that Act.

Companies, trusts, trustees of unit trust schemes, collective investment schemes, foundations and non-resident sociétés pay income tax on chargeable income. Chargeable income is gross income less allowable deductions. Gross income is all income other than exempt income.

rows: Standard rate
Company exporting goods
3% on the chargeable income attributable to exports. That share is gross income from exports divided by total gross income, multiplied by chargeable income
Freeport operator or private freeport developer manufacturing goods for the local market
3%, subject to prescribed substance conditions
Manufacturing company in the medical, biotechnology or pharmaceutical sector holding an Investment Certificate from the Economic Development Board
3%, subject to prescribed conditions
Higher education institution set up in Mauritius

items: Export of goods includes international buying and selling where the goods go straight from the exporting country to the importing country without landing in Mauritius, and the sale of aviation fuel to an airline. Since the Finance Act 2026 it no longer includes the export of live animals.

A partial exemption takes 80% of some kinds of income out of tax. The table below lists them. The company must carry out its core income generating activities in Mauritius, employ enough suitably qualified people and incur a minimum level of expenditure. Expenditure incurred to earn exempt income cannot be deducted.

A loss can be carried forward and set against net income of the following 5 income years, provided there is no change of more than 50% in the shareholding. The 5 year limit does not apply to the part of a loss that comes from annual allowance on capital expenditure incurred on or after 1 July 2006.

rows: Foreign dividends received by a company other than a bank, where the dividend was not deducted in the country it came from

Interest earned by a company other than a bank, a non-bank deposit taker, a money changer, a foreign exchange dealer, an insurer, a leasing company or a company providing factoring, hire purchase or credit sales
Interest earned by a collective investment scheme or a closed-end fund
Other income of a collective investment scheme or closed-end fund, and the income of a licensed fund manager, fund administrator, investment adviser, investment dealer or asset manager
Profit of a permanent establishment that a resident company has abroad
Leasing of ships, aircraft, locomotives and trains. Reinsurance and reinsurance brokering. Leasing and provision of international fibre capacity. Sale, financing and asset management of aircraft
Interest from money lent through a licensed peer-to-peer lending platform

Income of a company holding a licence from the Financial Services Commission for payment intermediary services, for robotic and artificial intelligence enabled advisory services, or as a virtual asset service provider

blocks.text: An alternative minimum tax applies from the year of assessment starting 1 July 2026. It covers companies operating a hotel, insurance companies, financial intermediaries, companies in real estate activities and licensed telecommunication companies. Where the normal tax is less than 10% of adjusted book profit, the tax payable is 10% of adjusted book profit. Global business entities are excluded.

sections.heading: CSR, the climate levy and the Fair Share Contribution

blocks.text: Every company must set up a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Fund each year equal to 2% of its chargeable income of the previous year. Companies holding a Global Business Licence, foundations, trusts and non-resident sociétés are outside the rule, as is a company that elected to pay presumptive tax for the previous income year. Part of the Fund is paid to the MRA. The rest is spent on a CSR programme, or given to a non-governmental organisation running one, in the priority areas listed in the Act. A company that files APS statements pays the MRA share in four parts: 25% with each of the first three APS statements and 25% with the annual return. Other companies pay with the annual return. Tax credits cannot be set against CSR.

columns: Share to be paid to the MRA
rows: 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2025
At least 75%
1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026
At least 50%
On or after 1 January 2027
At least 75%

items: The Corporate Climate Responsibility (CCR) levy is 2% of chargeable income. It applies from the year of assessment that started on 1 July 2024.
No CCR levy is due for a year in which the company's turnover is MUR 50 million or less. Turnover here means gross income from all sources, including exempt income.

Since the Finance Act 2026 a company that files APS statements pays the CCR levy quarterly with those statements, and the balance with its annual return. Other companies pay it with the annual return.

The quarterly CCR amount is reduced by 75% where the APS due date falls between 1 July 2026 and 30 June 2027. The reduction is 50% between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, and 25% between 1 July 2028 and 30 June 2029.

A company with chargeable income above MUR 24 million in an accounting year pays a Fair Share Contribution. The rate is 5% of chargeable income for a company taxed at 15% and 2% for a company taxed at 3%.
The contribution applies to income derived from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028. Global business entities are excluded.
The Finance Act 2026 removed the earlier test based on supplies and VAT registration, so chargeable income is the only test.

The company files a Fair Share Contribution statement and pays electronically each quarter. Statements for the first three quarters are due within 3 months of the end of the month in which the quarter ends. The fourth covers the whole accounting year and is due within 6 months of the year end.
Late payment of the contribution carries a penalty of 2.5% and interest of 0.25% a month.

blocks.text: A sole trader is taxed as an individual. The MRA treats as self-employed a person who has no contract of employment and derives income from a trade, business or profession in their own name, or from rent. The income year runs from 1 July to 30 June, and the return is due by 15 October. An individual doing business in Mauritius obtains a Business Registration Number from the Corporate and Business Registration Department and shows it on every invoice.

rows: First MUR 500,000
Next MUR 500,000
Next MUR 11 million
Remainder

items: For the income year that started on 1 July 2025 an individual also pays a Fair Share Contribution of 15% on leviable income above MUR 12 million. The Finance Act 2026 limited that contribution to that one income year.
The 35% band applies to the income year starting 1 July 2026 and to every later income year.

Chargeable income is worked out after reliefs and deductions. The deduction for dependents is MUR 110,000 for one dependent, MUR 190,000 for two, MUR 275,000 for three and MUR 355,000 for four or more. Our guide to personal income tax sets out the others.

A self-employed person also pays the Contribution Sociale Généralisée (CSG) on net income. It is MUR 150 a month where monthly net income is MUR 10,000 or less. Between MUR 10,000 and MUR 50,000 it is 1.5% of 90% of net income, with a minimum of MUR 150. Above MUR 50,000 it is 3% of 90% of net income.

blocks.text: The Income Tax Act calls a partnership a société. The word covers a société formed under the law of Mauritius, a société de fait or en participation, a limited partnership, a limited liability partnership, a joint venture and a partnership formed abroad. A société is resident where its seat is in Mauritius, or where at least one associate or manager is resident. A resident société pays no income tax. Each associate is taxed on a share of its income, whether or not that share is paid out: an individual on the bands for individuals, a company at its own rate.

items: The société itself sets up a CSR Fund of 2% of its net income of the previous year, unless it holds a Global Business Licence. It also pays the CCR levy, at 2% of its net income, when its turnover is above MUR 50 million.
It files a return by 30 September after the income year and gives each associate a statement of the share that falls to them.
A non-resident société is taxed as a company, at 15%.
The Fair Share Contribution is charged on companies. Its definition of a company names a non-resident société and does not name a resident one.

blocks.text: A small enterprise can elect to pay a presumptive tax of 1% of its gross income in place of tax on chargeable income. The election is made by irrevocable notice on or before the due date of the return. Three conditions apply.

items: The business is engaged in agriculture, forestry and fishing, manufacturing other than restaurants, retail of goods (including food sold to be eaten off the premises) or wholesale of goods.
Its gross income in the income year is MUR 10 million or less.
Its gross income from other sources is MUR 400,000 or less.

blocks.text: A business that elects cannot claim deductions, reliefs or allowances. It files a return by the normal due date and pays the tax with it, less any tax already withheld under PAYE or deducted at source. Where the MRA finds undeclared gross income and the total stays within MUR 10 million, it can charge presumptive tax on the undeclared amount.
An individual engaged in these activities whose gross income for the previous year was MUR 10 million or less does not file quarterly CPS statements.

sections.heading: Paying during the year: APS, CPS and tax deducted at source

blocks.text: Under the Advance Payment System (APS) a company files a statement and pays tax for each of the first three quarters of its accounting year. No statement is due for a quarter where, in the previous accounting year, gross income was MUR 10 million or less or the company had no chargeable income. The company chooses how to work out the chargeable income of a quarter: 25% of the previous year's chargeable income, or the actual gross income less allowable deductions for the quarter. Tax is charged at the company's own rate. APS is a provisional payment and is set against the tax due on the annual return.

rows: First, second and third quarter of the accounting year
Within 3 months of the end of the month in which the quarter ends
Quarter ending in March
2 days, excluding Saturdays and public holidays, before the end of June
Quarter ending in September
2 days, excluding Saturdays and public holidays, before the end of December

blocks.text: Under the Current Payment System (CPS) an individual with business or rental income files a quarterly statement and pays tax. The quarter July to September is due 2 days, excluding Saturdays and public holidays, before the end of December. October to December is due on 31 March. January to March is due 2 days, excluding Saturdays and public holidays, before the end of June. No statement is due where gross income under CPS in the previous income year was MUR 4 million or less, or where the tax for the quarter is MUR 500 or less.

items: Some payments to a business have tax deducted at source (TDS) by the payer, who sends it to the MRA. It is an advance payment and is set against the recipient's income tax.

Rates include 0.75% on payments to contractors and sub-contractors, 3% on commission and 7.5% on rent paid to a resident. The rate is 5% on fees for the professional services listed in the Fifth Schedule to the Income Tax Act.
No tax is deducted where the amount would be less than MUR 500.

The Finance Act 2026 added two items. One is 1% on payments above MUR 300,000 made by a person other than an individual to an ICT services provider for software, software licences and related maintenance. The other is 5% on payments made by a person other than an individual for advertising, promotional, endorsement or marketing services carried out through social media or digital content.

blocks.text: The MRA identifies taxpayers by a Tax Account Number (TAN). A company uses its TAN as the user ID to file returns on MRA e-services, with a password issued by the MRA. An individual logs in with a National Identity Card number, a Non-Citizen Identity Card number or a TAN.

Every company must file its annual return and pay its tax electronically, through MRA e-services or the Mauritius Network Services system. A company that does not do so after written notice from the MRA is liable to a penalty. It is 20% of the tax payable, up to MUR 100,000, or MUR 5,000 where the return shows no tax.

A company can ask an approved e-Filing Service Centre to file on its behalf. Payment by direct debit needs a PLACH Direct Debit Mandate Form, which must reach the MRA at least 15 days before the payment date.
Individuals also file and pay electronically. A self-employed person who is not required to file the standard return files a simplified return.

items: An individual files a return where any one of these applies in the income year: total net income above MUR 500,000, gross income from business above MUR 2 million, PAYE withheld from emoluments, tax deducted at source from income, or chargeable income.
A person who has to file once keeps filing each year unless the MRA agrees otherwise in writing.

A company that is not in operation can submit a declaration of company not in operation in place of a return. MRA guidance sets a limit of 3 months from the end of the accounting year for that declaration.

The MRA publishes a tax calendar listing each month's due dates. In 2026, companies with a December 2025 year end had until Friday 26 June 2026, and companies with a June 2026 year end have until Tuesday 29 December 2026.

blocks.text: The MRA can move a date in a given year. In July 2026 it gave companies with a January 2026 year end until 31 August 2026 to file and pay. The e-filing facility for the year of assessment 2026-2027 was to open only after the Finance Bill 2026 was enacted.

Anyone carrying on business must keep proper books, registers, accounts, receipts, invoices, vouchers, contracts and a full record of transactions, in English or French, on computer or on paper. Records are kept for at least 5 years after the transaction. An employer also keeps records of pay and tax withheld, and employees' declaration forms.

MUR 2,000 for each month or part of a month, up to MUR 20,000. Up to MUR 5,000 for a small enterprise with turnover of MUR 10 million or less, or an individual not in business

2.5% of the tax. 1% for a small enterprise with turnover of MUR 10 million or less, or an individual not in business

blocks.text: The Finance Act 2025 halved the late payment penalty and the interest rate with effect from 1 July 2025. The penalty went from 5% to 2.5%, and from 2% to 1% for small enterprises. Interest went from 0.5% to 0.25% a month. On 20 November 2026 the MRA's corporate taxation, APS and self-employed pages still showed the old rates. This guide follows the Income Tax Act as consolidated up to the Finance Act 2026 and the MRA's Penalty and Interest page, which show the new rates.

items: A taxpayer who is in doubt about how the law applies to an item can state the doubt in the return. The taxpayer is then treated as having acted in good faith, and no late payment penalty is charged on extra tax that results from that item.
Where a company does not file a return, the MRA can issue an automatic tax claim payable within 28 days.
The MRA can also publish the name of a company that has not filed on its website, no sooner than 3 months after the due date and after 7 days' notice.

unverified: The rate at which tax is charged on a quarterly CPS statement. Section 108 of the Income Tax Act leaves the method to regulations. The MRA self-employed page gives 15%, but that page also shows penalty rates that were replaced on 1 July 2025, so the figure was left out. The MRA copy of the Income Tax Regulations 1996, consolidated to April 2026, was searched without finding the CPS computation.
How and when a Tax Account Number is first allotted to a newly registered company or sole trader. The MRA pages fetched show how a TAN is used to log in and file, not how it is issued.

MRA guidance on how the alternative minimum tax (year of assessment starting 1 July 2026) is reported in APS statements and the annual return. Only the text of section 44A of the Income Tax Act was found.

MRA guidance for individuals on the 35% band that applies from the income year starting 1 July 2026. The band is confirmed in the Finance Act 2026 and the consolidated Income Tax Act, and in KPMG's summary, but the MRA individual pages and tax calculator still showed the 2025-2026 rates on 20 November 2026.

Whether the MRA page figures for tax deducted at source are complete and current for late 2026. The rates quoted were read from the MRA TDS page, and the two items added in 2026 from the Finance Act 2026. The full Sixth Schedule was not compared line by line.
The substance conditions prescribed for the 3% rate for freeport manufacturing and for medical, biotechnology and pharmaceutical manufacturing. They sit in regulations that were not fetched.

How the Fair Share Contribution is charged on a company taxed partly at 3% and partly at 15%. Section 53N of the VAT Act gives 5% for a company subject to tax at 15% and 2% for one subject to tax at 3%. Neither it nor the MRA page says how a company that exports only part of its goods is treated.
